merge.title: Per-boot refuse-only SE configuration audit over authenticated, fresh channels, with SE identity proven host-side against a factory per-unit record (no on-device classical verify, no DHUK-keyed attestation)
merge.threat: Three distinct attackers, which the members blurred together. (T1) A secure element whose access conditions are looser than designed: lockdown skipped at the factory, re-provisioned in transit while S-1/S-2/S-3 are still open, or a known-weak AC nobody would notice (OP17-1: F1D1..F1D4 are Read=Auto(F1D0) alone today). Firmware reads metadata only inside provision_* paths, so such a device boots and unlocks normally. (T2) Chip substitution or clone board: wrong SE050 variant (E2 vs C2 already hit on the bench), a transplanted genuine SE, or an emulator. After first-boot rotation a swapped chip already fails the PBS/SCP03 handshake, so the real exposure is before first boot, when the transport keys are derivable from OTP that is SWD-readable at RDP-0. (T3) An I2C interposer that forces the OPTIGA driver into its plaintext branch or replays a recorded Shielded session, making any on-device readback worthless. Not addressed by this cluster: malicious firmware on genuine chips, and board implants.
merge.proposal:
One recommendation in three ordered layers. Device-side verdicts are refuse-and-park only.

L0, channel prerequisites (firmware, S). Without these the audit is replayable or bypassable.
- Remove the silent plaintext fallback in optiga::apdu::send_command (secure/src/optiga/apdu.rs:523-533). Replace it with an explicit allowlist of pre-shield commands: OpenApplication, the Read=ALW counter probe in check_provisioned, and the pairing-window PBS write. Everything else returns Err(Shield) when shield.active is false (#126).
- Add a freshness step after ensure_shield: one command carrying 32 B of fresh TRNG whose CCM-authenticated response is required before any identity or config verdict. The Infineon PRL has no host-nonce slot (shield.rs:386-388), so this is the only available replacement (#117).
- Take verdicts only from shield-active or SCP03-authenticated reads, never from the pre-shield check_provisioned window or from bare status words (#120, #121).

L1, per-boot configuration audit (firmware, M). Merges SE-04 with IMP-05 step 3.
- Run after both tunnels are up and before check_provisioned/unlock, in the main.rs window between SE init and nsc::reconcile_pin_attempts (main.rs:1751-1801).
- OPTIGA: get_metadata for E140, E120, F1D0..F1D4, the type-0x11 pool {E0E8, E0E9, E0EF}, E0E0..E0E3, plus F1D8/E121 and the duress twins under duress-pin. Compare tag-wise (Change/Read/Execute/DataType, as metadata_matches_expected at apdu.rs:1544 does, plus LcsO where the profile expects Operational) against a per-OID allowlist of accepted encodings, versioned by lifecycle profile. Use allowlisted encodings, not a "looser than" order: OPTIGA ACs are expression TLVs, not bitmasks. The table must mirror what is actually provisioned today and gain the S-1/S-2/S-3 end-state rows when those close.
- SE050: get_version_ext inside the SCP03 session, with AppletConfig and applet version pinned as firmware constants (not learned at first boot); existence and type of UserID, admin and half_E objects; ReadObjectAttributes only where policy permits; LockState == Active (#63).
- Any mismatch is a hard refusal with a readable error code. Never wipe, never auto-tighten or self-heal.
- Put the comparator and table in a host-testable workspace crate, because secure/src modules are excluded from host tests. Generate docs/secure-elements/optiga-expected-metadata.md from the same table and diff it in `make invariant-gates`.
- On rdp2-self-lock builds, journal the expected-table version in page 127; bench/QEMU builds use the compile-time table only.

L2, identity (mixed, L). Lives inside #249, not as a parallel design.
- Factory per-unit record (birth certificate, transparency log) carries the OPTIGA E0C2 UID, sha256 of the E0E0 device cert, and the SE050 UID/chipId; an OTP anchor of that tuple is burned with the transport OTP so the SWD pre-power verifier covers it.
- The device compares live UIDs to the OTP anchor each boot (refuse-only). This catches non-emulating swaps and gives a labelled "SE IDENTITY MISMATCH" instead of a generic auth error.
- The anti-emulator proof is host-side: a companion/WebUSB verifier sends a nonce, each SE signs with its own vendor attestation key (OPTIGA E0F0; SE050 attestation key), and the firmware only relays under a domain-separated tag. The host verifies each chain against that element's own vendor root and cross-checks the birth record (per-element binding, per the Trezor 2026-08 fix).
- No ECDSA verification and no vendor root live in the secure image.

Also correct the docs that present boot attestation as existing: HARDENING.md §3.4, :32, :176, the CLAUDE.md Lifecycle line, and the main.rs:1598 comment.

members.note: Backbone of the merge; passed all three round-1 lenses. Kept: per-boot config readback against a pinned table, plaintext-fallback removal, host-side chain verification with per-element roots. Changed per round-1 corrections: identity pin must be factory-issued, not learned at first boot; SE050 UserID attribute readback is infeasible (0x6986); the host handshake nonce is replaced by a fresh-TRNG authenticated command; wipe-on-mismatch becomes refuse-only; 'refuse on looser' becomes a per-OID allowlist of encodings. Precedent corrected: Trezor's TROPIC check is write-to-fix, and Trezor has no per-boot Optiga check.

No round-1 verify; verified here. No boot-path metadata audit exists: every get_metadata caller in secure/src/optiga/mod.rs is a provision/lock/duress-liveness path (:898 is dead_code, :1087 is verify_and_lock, :3174 is liveness only). The helpers exist (apdu.rs:1522, 1544, 1603). SE050 check_provisioned is existence-only (se050/mod.rs:1788-1796). Its own risk notes already match the round-1 corrections (0x6986 on UserID, park not wipe, no self-heal). Adopted nearly whole as layer L1. Adjustments: comparator moves to a host-testable crate; the F1E1 row waits on #14/#215; a freshness step is required before any verdict.

No round-1 verify; verified here. Absence confirmed: no E0C2/E0E0 read in secure/src, get_version_ext is harness-only (se050_stress/ctx.rs:505), nothing in main.rs:1570-1801 or first_boot checks identity. Doc drift confirmed. Kept: per-element comparison, refuse-not-wipe, and the E0C2 / E0E0 / SE050-version identity tuple. Dropped: first-boot self-pin as the security mechanism, the DHUK-CMAC seal, the optional C10 MCU attestation, and the OEF 0xA921 pin (#206 says OEF is not in GetVersion; pin AppletConfig). P0 is not justified: after rotation a swapped chip already fails the handshake.

No round-1 verify; verified here. Absence confirmed: no attestation CMD in proto/src/lib.rs, die_id.rs only decodes IDCODE and its own header says a matching IDCODE proves nothing, threat-model.md:339-345 and :505 say not landed. Kept: factory-pinned UIDs with an OTP anchor (already the #249 plan) and a fresh-nonce SE proof, but verified by the host, not the device. Dropped: on-device ECDSA verification of vendor chains, CMD_ATTEST_DEVICE with a DHUK-derived C10 key, binding to the FSBL measurement, and mismatch routed to admin-wipe.

dropped_parts: On-device verification of Infineon/NXP ECDSA chains with roots pinned in the image (BOOT-05; also the literal text of #210, #244, #245). Invariant #5 allows classical verification only in host dbgen, and scripts/check_classical_crypto_boundary.py fails if any workspace member other than dbgen/xtask reaches k256/ecdsa. docs/security/user-device-verification.md:24-34 records that no on-device answer can distinguish fake firmware, and keeps the SE-CA check as a companion-side control. No vendor verifies SE vendor chains on device; Trezor does it in trezorlib/Suite. It would also need P-256 (and likely larger curves for the Infineon root, unconfirmed) in a slot with 34 KB headroom.

CMD_ATTEST_DEVICE signing with a C10 key derived from SAES-CMAC(DHUK,'attest') and certified by the factory (BOOT-05 step 2, SE-01 optional step). Three independent refutations: (i) the factory never runs at RDP-2 and DHUK is final only after first-boot self-lock, so the factory cannot certify the key (#249 states a per-die DHUK fingerprint is impossible under #36); (ii) fact (d): any secure-world image can select DHUK via SAES KEYSEL, so the key proves 'some secure image on this die', not a genuine image; (iii) Trezor's own ML-DSA MCU attestation was walked back host-side (8bc6d1b28b; trezor-comparison.md D1) and #249 records that lesson. Cost is also poor: a C10 sign is 6.4-7.2 s on pq1 with a cached key, more with per-use keygen, plus a 4008 B signature over 64 B HID.

Binding the attestation to the FSBL-forwarded measurement (BOOT-05 step 3). It depends on an FSBL handoff secret hidden by HDP that does not exist (fact d), and the FSBL size/boot budget is the recorded NO-GO for new FSBL work. Without the hidden secret, a malicious secure image fabricates the digest.

DHUK-CMAC seal over the identity record in page 127 (SE-01). At RDP-2, flash is not externally writable and any secure image can recompute CMAC_DHUK (fact d), so the seal adds nothing over a plain journal record.

First-boot self-pinning as the defence against transit swap (IMP-05 steps 1-2, SE-01). It enshrines whichever chip is present at first boot; after first boot a swapped chip already fails the rotated PBS/SCP03 handshake. Retained only as an optional labelled diagnostic; the security anchor is the factory record.

Wipe, admin-wipe or 'permanent lockdown' on mismatch (IMP-05 step 2, BOOT-05 step 1, threat-model §7.11 wording). Status paths on both channels are unauthenticated (SE10, #120), so a single forged frame would become a wipe lever; a swapped-away SE takes its XOR half with it, so wiping the remaining chip only harms the owner.
Host nonce in the OPTIGA Shielded handshake (IMP-05 step 4b). The PRL has only random_S (shield.rs:386-388). Replaced by a fresh-TRNG authenticated command.
'Persistent across two reads' as the anti-interposer gate (IMP-05 risks). A replaying interposer passes it. Replaced by the freshness command.
SE050 ReadObjectAttributes/policy compare on the production UserID (IMP-05 step 3). Silicon returns 0x6986 (se050/mod.rs:834-872; invariant #2). Coverage of that object is existence/type only.

Pinning SE050 OEF 0xA921 via GetVersion (SE-01, #61) or learning the applet version at first boot (IMP-05). #206 records that OEF is not in GetVersion; pin AppletConfig and applet version as firmware constants once #697 names the production part.

Porting Trezor's boot-time self-heal/auto-tighten (optiga_set_metadata, tropic_ensure_i_config). Owner decision: ordinary pairing must never ratchet E140, and LcsO moves are irreversible factory ceremonies (S-1/S-2/S-3 deferred by design).

'Refuse on looser, accept tighter' as a strictness partial order on OPTIGA metadata (IMP-05, SE-04). ACs are expression TLVs; a strictness evaluator is extra unproven code. Use bit-exact tag compare against an allowlist of accepted encodings per OID.

Cited sources that do not support the claim (IMP-05): arXiv 2608.17082 is an I2C sensor-bus paper with no wallet/SE content, and the Donjon Safe 3 page has no Optiga metadata content. The 'batch-ID allowlist' and 'silicon-revision gate' are not Trezor boot identity gates.

4. A domain-separated relay command that lets each SE sign a host nonce, without becoming a general signing oracle.
5. The doc drift: HARDENING.md §3.4, :32 and :176, the CLAUDE.md Lifecycle line and the main.rs:1598 comment describe a boot attestation step that does not exist, while threat-model.md §9.4 says it has not landed.
6. Placing the comparator in a host-testable crate with a negative control per OID, and journaling the expected-table version in page 127.
An umbrella issue linking #210, #206, #61, #63, #27, #126, #117 and #120 would replace the current scatter; #61 and #206 should be merged.

merge.rationale:
Priority P1, not SE-01's P0. After first-boot rotation a swapped chip already fails the handshake, and before first boot no on-device check can beat an attacker who holds the OTP-derived transport keys, so the identity pin is not the ship-critical piece. The parts with real security value are L0 and L1: together they turn the S-1/S-2/S-3 lockdown from a one-time factory act into a property re-checked every boot, and they are the only detector for a skipped or weakened lockdown.

Cost splits: L0 is S, L1 is M (glue over existing primitives get_metadata, metadata_matches_expected, get_version_ext, and the page-127 journal), L2 is L and already sits under ship-blocker #249. Overall L. L0 and L1 are firmware-only and can land before any factory decision.

Novelty is parity because Trezor ships per-boot TROPIC config checking and Trezor, Ledger and BitBox ship host-verified attestation; the refuse-only dual-SE audit is the part that goes beyond.

Not done: the advisor tool was rate-limited and the codex MCP was down, so no second-model review ran on this reconciliation. Boot-time cost, flash cost, and E0C2/E0E0/E0F0 access at the shipping lifecycle state are estimates or unconfirmed.

merge.residual_after:
What an attacker can still do once all three layers land:
- Malicious firmware on genuine chips passes everything; the firmware proof remains the SWD pre-power verification and the FSBL fingerprint, not this.
- A pre-first-boot attacker who reads OTP over SWD derives the transport keys and can passively decrypt the first-boot rotation from an I2C tap, learning the final PBS and SCP03 keys; identity and config checks do not see this. It is the open #76/#268 handoff gate.
- An emulator or interposer that already holds the final credentials passes every on-device check. Only the host-side vendor-key challenge catches an emulator, and only if the user runs it.
- Board implants on the display SPI or buttons are invisible to SE attestation, as Ledger states for its own check.
- An interposer can still force a refusal (denial of service), though no longer a wipe through this path.
- A compromised factory HSM or provisioning station mints valid birth records until the transparency log exists (#68).
- The audit detects loose access conditions but cannot fix them: a unit that fails is parked, and the S-1/S-2/S-3 ceremonies remain the actual lockdown.
- SE050 UserID policy (max attempts, policy bytes) stays unverifiable at boot because attribute reads are denied.

skeptic.reason:
The core survives: a refuse-only config audit plus host-side SE identity, with no on-device classical verify and no DHUK-keyed attestation, is consistent with invariant #5, the #36 shipping model and user-device-verification.md:24-34. The absence claims check out (no E0C2/E0E0 read, no boot audit, get_version_ext harness-only). It is not refuted, but it needs seven substantive corrections.

1. **The L0 freshness step is unsound as written.** A replayed PRL session yields the same keys and sequence numbers, so a recorded response still passes CCM. "A CCM-authenticated response is required" proves nothing unless the response content is a function of the host nonce. No such command exists in the driver: apdu.rs exposes only get_random, get/set data and metadata, hmac_verify, generate_auth_code and protected_update. There is no CalcHash or echo.

2. **L1's placement and value are overstated.** The secret objects F1D0..F1D4 are created by the firmware in the seed wizard and already checked by verify_and_lock, not by the factory. The gap that actually exists is the already-Operational skip (optiga/mod.rs:1276-1287 and :1087-1093), which writes the secret first and then trusts frozen metadata. A boot audit "before unlock" fires only on the next boot, after the secret is already sitting in the loose object.

3. **That gap is tracked as #87, which the merge missed, and #87 carries an owner deferral.** Failing closed on a frozen, unfixable object is recorded there as a security-versus-brick tradeoff awaiting sacrificial silicon. L1's refuse-and-park is the same tradeoff applied on every boot.

4. **The audit as ordered would refuse every fresh unit.** Running it "before check_provisioned" leaves no authenticated way to tell a blank or factory-reset chip from a provisioned one, and the table has no row for either state.

5. **Live defect 1's cited trigger is stale.** unwrap_response (shield.rs:558-660) no longer clears `active`. The fallback is unconditional, but I found no ship-path secret read that reaches it.

6. **#249's own body specifies on-device E0F0 chain verification against a pinned Infineon root.** "L2 lives inside #249" therefore inherits the invariant #5 conflict the merge attributes only to #210/#244/#245.

7. **Journaling the table version in page 127 adds persistent state with no stated consumer.** It also creates a firmware-update mismatch hazard on a page invariant #3 reserves for the first-boot journal and salt.

Residual after all layers: an interposer or emulator holding final credentials, or any attacker before first boot with the OTP-derived transport keys, passes every on-device check. Only the optional host challenge catches an emulator.
skeptic.corrections:
**L0 (channel prerequisites)**
- Specify the freshness command so the host verifies nonce-dependent content, for example CalcHash over 32 B of TRNG compared with a local SHA-256, or a scratch-object write then read-back (which costs NVM wear). Either needs a new APDU wrapper; none exists in secure/src/optiga/apdu.rs. L0 is S-to-M, not S.
- Freshness applies to OPTIGA only. SE050 SCP03 already carries a host challenge, and se050 send_apdu refuses without a session (se050/apdu.rs:308-310), so there is no SE050 plaintext fallback.
- Re-base the plaintext-fallback item on current code. The #126 trigger (sequence threshold checked before the tag in unwrap_response) is gone: shield.rs:558-660 returns Err without touching `active`. `active=false` is now set only by host-side wrap_command (shield.rs:460-522) and by driver reset/error handlers (optiga/mod.rs:265, 313, 960, 994, 2752). Ship-path entry points call ensure_shield first (e.g. mod.rs:358, 2390, 3165, 3261). Keep the allowlist as defence in depth, not as a demonstrated plaintext-secret path.
- The allowlist must also cover setup_pbs_no_handshake (mod.rs:848-854) and ensure_pbs_lcso_operational (mod.rs:898-908), which intentionally run pre-shield.

**L1 (configuration audit)**
- Add a provisioning-time check: read metadata before writing any secret, and when the object is already Operational, compare and refuse on mismatch (mod.rs:1276-1287, 1087-1093). The per-boot audit alone misses the write-time window. This is #87 and needs the owner's brick-tradeoff decision; do not present L1 as decision-free.
- Add table rows for the blank/pre-wizard state and the factory-reset-sentinel state, selected by an authenticated discriminator. check_provisioned is a plaintext Read=ALW probe (mod.rs:945-1000, #121) and cannot be that discriminator as it stands.
- Fix the ordering. On rdp2-self-lock builds the first SE traffic is first_boot::run_post_lock_provisioning (main.rs:1753-1764) and load_pbs follows (main.rs:1766-1783). The audit can only run after both, and must state which keyset it uses when rotation is mid-journal.
- The real T1 value is in the factory-owned rows (E140 LcsO, the type-0x11 pool, E0E0..E0E3), which are undefined until S-1/S-2/S-3 close. Vendor-default metadata for those objects varies by batch, so survey silicon before making them refuse-and-park, or the audit bricks legitimate units.
- Drop the page-127 table-version journal, or name its consumer and the firmware-update behaviour.
- The SE050 LockState assert needs a new ReadState APDU. No LockState reader exists in secure/src/se050; add it to the cost.
- Add an explicit note that a firmware update shipping a wrong table parks the whole fleet. Funds stay recoverable by seed, but it must be rehearsed against the A/B rollback path.

**L2 (identity)**
- Add #249 to the issues needing retargeting; its body specifies the on-device E0F0 chain check.
- Gate the relay command behind an on-device confirm. E0C2 plus the E0E0 certificate is a stable device identifier exposed to any USB host.
- The OTP-anchor UID compare uses Read=ALW plaintext identifiers. Label it a diagnostic, not a security control.

**Docs**
- The main.rs:1598 comment is weak evidence: it sits inside a bench se-i2c-probe block and merely lists boot steps. HARDENING.md:176, 178-189, :32 and CLAUDE.md:48 are the real drift.

**Priority**
- Split it: the L0 freshness work (#117, #120, #121) stays P1 under its own issues; L1 is P2 until #87 and the S-row decisions land; L2 remains under ship-blocker #249.

**Not checked**
- I did not trace every provisioning-path caller for a mid-function un-shielded command. The ship-path claim rests on the entry points listed above.
- #444's wire shape is confirmed by reading the code; whether the chip rejects it is still silicon-pending.
- E0C2/E0E0/E0F0 access at the shipping lifecycle state remains unconfirmed, as the merge says.

L1's refuse-and-park on frozen objects is the same tradeoff applied every boot and cannot land as decision-free firmware work.

Invariant #5 versus #249's own text: #249 specifies boot-time E0F0 signing chained to a pinned Infineon root on the device. Placing L2 inside #249 without retargeting it re-imports the conflict the merge resolved for #210, #244 and #245.
